parts.latex:
A bag contains 150 jelly beans. Some of them are red and the rest are blue. The ratio of red to blue jelly beans is $2:3$.

Sophie eats 10 of each colour.

What is the new ratio of red to blue jelly beans?

solutions.latex:
The ratio $2:3$ has $2+3=5$ parts, so each part is $150\div 5 = 30$ jelly beans.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{red} &= 2\times 30 = 60\\ \text{blue} &= 3\times 30 = 90 \end{aligned}$$
After Sophie eats 10 of each colour:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{red} &= 50\\ \text{blue} &= 80 \end{aligned}$$
The new ratio is
$$50:80 = 5:8$$
This is option C.

4387.stem:
Kim is building a path around a garden at the back of a house, as shown. The path is 0.5 m wide.

\exfigure{300_q26_1}

parts.latex: Find the area of the path.

Kim is mixing some concrete for the path. The concrete mix is made up of crushed rock, sand and cement in the ratio of $4:2:1$ by weight.

Kim needs 2.1 tonnes of concrete mix in the correct ratio.

Calculate how many 15 kg bags of cement Kim needs to buy.

solutions.latex:
The path area is the area of the outer rectangle less the area of the inner rectangle.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area of path} &= (3\times 8)-(7\times 2.5)\\ &= 24-17.5\\ &= 6.5 \text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to calculate the area of the path, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The ratio of rock to sand to cement is $4:2:1$, so cement is $\dfrac{1}{7}$ of the mix.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount of cement} &= \dfrac{1}{7}\times 2.1 \text{ tonnes}\\ &= 0.3 \text{ tonnes}\\ &= 300 \text{ kg}\end{aligned}$$
Each bag holds 15 kg.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Number of bags} &= \dfrac{300}{15}\\ &= 20\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Kim needs 20 bags of cement.}$$
criteria: Calculates the weight of cement required, or equivalent merit
Identifies the proportion of cement in the mixture, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Lily wanted to estimate the number of fish in a lake.

She randomly captured 30 fish, then tagged and released them.

One week later she randomly captured 40 fish from the same lake. She found that 12 of these 40 fish were tagged.

What is the best estimate for the total number of fish in the lake?

solutions.latex:
Using the capture-recapture method, the proportion of tagged fish in the second sample estimates the proportion in the whole lake.

Let $N$ be the number of fish in the lake.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{12}{40}&=\dfrac{30}{N}\\ N&=\dfrac{30\times 40}{12}\\ &=100 \end{aligned}$$
So the best estimate is 100, option D.

meta.generated_note: Generated worked solution for MCQ; key D from option key.

parts.latex: What is 20 minutes to one-third of a day, expressed as a ratio in simplest form?

solutions.latex:
Express both quantities in the same unit.

One-third of a day is:
$$\dfrac{1}{3}\times 24=8\text{ hours}=8\times 60=480\text{ minutes}$$
The ratio is then:
$$\begin{aligned} 20:480&=1:24 \end{aligned}$$
(dividing both parts by 20).

So the answer is option B.

parts.latex:
A full container has 4.8 L of a mixture of cordial and water in the ratio $1 : 3$.

After removing 1.2 L of the mixture, more water is added to refill the container.

What is the ratio of cordial to water in the final mixture?

solutions.latex:
After removing 1.2 L, $3.6$ L remains, still in the ratio $1:3$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cordial} &= \dfrac{3.6}{4} = 0.9 \text{ L} \\ \text{Water} &= \dfrac{3.6\times 3}{4} = 2.7 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
Adding 1.2 L of water gives $2.7 + 1.2 = 3.9$ L of water.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{cordial} : \text{water} &= 0.9 : 3.9 \\ &= 3 : 13 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the ratio of cordial to water is } 3:13$$
criteria: Calculates the amount of cordial and of water in the mixture of 3.6 L
Attempts to apply the ratio $1:3$ to the mixture of 3.6 L

4501.stem: In a tropical drink, the ratio of pineapple juice to mango juice to orange juice is $15:9:4$.

figures.cap: rectangular prism 40 cm by 20 cm by 35 cm

parts.latex: How much orange juice is needed if the tropical drink is to contain 3 litres of pineapple juice?

solutions.latex:
Pineapple juice is 15 parts, so
$$1 \text{ part} = \dfrac{3}{15} \text{ L}$$
Orange juice is 4 parts:
$$4 \times \dfrac{3}{15} = 0.8 \text{ L}$$
$$\therefore\ 0.8 \text{ L (800 mL) of orange juice is required}$$
criteria: Identifies a relevant ratio, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Capacity of the container:
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 40 \times 20 \times 35 \\ &= 28\,000 \text{ cm}^3 \\ &= 28 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
Total number of parts:
$$15 + 9 + 4 = 28$$
Mango juice is 9 parts:
$$\dfrac{9}{28} \times 28 = 9 \text{ L}$$
$$\therefore\ 9 \text{ L of mango juice is required}$$
criteria: Provides correct capacity of the container and attempts to calculate the amount of mango juice required
Provides correct volume of the container, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: A map has a scale of 1:5000. If Oak St is 800 m, what is the scaled distance of Oak St?

solutions.latex:
The scale $1:5000$ means $1$ unit on the map represents $5000$ units on the ground.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Map distance} &= \dfrac{800}{5000} \\ &= 0.16 \text{ m} \\ &= 160 \text{ mm} \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

parts.latex:
Amie is studying the butterfly population in a park. She initially catches and tags 20 butterflies, before releasing them back into the park. Later, she captures a sample of 40 butterflies, of which 5 are already tagged.

Based on this data what is the most likely estimate for the butterfly population in the park?

solutions.latex:
Capture–recapture: the proportion tagged in the sample equals the proportion tagged in the population.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{5}{40} &= \dfrac{20}{N} \\ N &= \dfrac{20\times 40}{5} \\ &= 160 \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

4543.stem:
A marmalade recipe requires 5 oranges, 2 lemons, and 800 grams of sugar per batch.

Adele decides to make a larger batch while maintaining the recipe's proportions. She uses 15 more oranges than lemons.

parts.latex: Determine the number of oranges Adele will need for this larger batch.
Using this information, calculate the total amount of sugar required for Adele's batch of marmalade.

solutions.latex:
Let $O$ be the number of oranges and $L$ the number of lemons. The recipe ratio gives $\dfrac{O}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$, and $O = L + 15$.
$$\dfrac{L+15}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 2L + 30 &= 5L \\ 3L &= 30 \\ L &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} O &= 10 + 15 \\ &= 25 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 25 \text{ oranges}$$

Sugar is in proportion to oranges.
$$\dfrac{800}{5} = 160 \text{ g of sugar per orange}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 25\times 160 &= 4000 \text{ g} \\ &= 4 \text{ kg} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 4 \text{ kg of sugar}$$

4545.stem:
\exfigure{722_q22_1}

The diagram above, drawn to scale on a 1 cm grid, represents an ocean pool located adjacent to the shoreline. The pool consists of a semicircular section and an irregularly shaped region. The entire pool has a uniform depth of 2 metres, and the scale of the diagram is 1:1000.

figures.cap: ocean pool on a 1 cm grid: semicircle plus irregular region beside shoreline

parts.latex: Use the trapezoidal rule with a single application to estimate the area of the irregular region.
Hence, show that the total capacity of the pool is 1900 kL, correct to 2 significant figures.

Initially, the ocean pool is filled with a mixture of fresh water and chlorinated water in the ratio 7:18. After some water is removed, 1000 kL remains. To refill the pool, 100 kL of fresh water is added first, and the remaining volume is restored to 1900 kL using chlorinated water.

Determine the new ratio of fresh water to chlorinated water after the refill.

solutions.latex:
Apply the trapezoidal rule with one application, $A \approx \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_l)$, with $h = 40$ m and the two end measurements $30$ m and $10$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} A &\approx \dfrac{40}{2}(30 + 10) \\ &= 800 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Values 40, 30, 10 taken from source (figure not viewed).

solutions.latex:
The volume is the total area times the depth of $2$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= (\text{semicircle} + \text{irregular region})\times \text{depth} \\ &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\times \pi\times 10^2 + 800\right)\times 2 \\ &= 1914.16\ldots \text{ m}^3 \\ &\approx 1900 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
Since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1 \text{ kL}$, the capacity is $1900$ kL to 2 significant figures.
criteria: Finds the total area or the volume, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The ratio $7:18$ has $25$ parts. Scale it to $1000$ kL.
$$7:18 = 280:720$$
After the refill the total is $1900$ kL. Fresh water is $280 + 100$ and chlorinated water is the rest.
$$\text{fresh} = 280 + 100 = 380 \text{ kL}$$
$$\text{chlorinated} = 1900 - 380 = 1520 \text{ kL}$$
$$380 : 1520 = 1 : 4$$
$$\therefore\ \text{New ratio} = 1:4$$
criteria: Finds the fresh and chlorinated volumes after the refill, or equivalent merit
Finds the fresh and chlorinated volumes in the $1000$ kL, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Scientists are studying a penguin colony in Antarctica. As part of the study, 28 penguins are captured, tagged and released back into the colony.

The following week, 50 penguins from the same colony are captured and it is found that 4 of these penguins are already tagged.

What is the best estimate of the total number of penguins in the colony?

solutions.latex:
The tagged proportion in the sample should match the tagged proportion in the colony. Let $p$ be the colony size.
$$\dfrac{28}{p} = \dfrac{4}{50}$$
$$\begin{aligned} p &= \dfrac{28 \times 50}{4} \\ &= 350 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{about } 350 \text{ penguins}$$

parts.latex:
On a map which is drawn to a scale of 1:2000, a park measures 2.5 cm by 3.5 cm.

In a recent storm, 15 mm of rain fell on the park.

Calculate the amount of water, in litres, that fell on the park.

solutions.latex:
The scale is $1:2000$, so $1 \text{ cm}$ represents $2000 \text{ cm} = 20 \text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned} 2.5 \times 20 &= 50 \text{ m} \\ 3.5 \times 20 &= 70 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
The depth of rain is $15 \text{ mm} = 0.015 \text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 50 \times 70 \times 0.015 \\ &= 52.5 \text{ m}^3 \\ &= 52\,500 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 52\,500 \text{ L}$$
criteria: Correct volume $52.5 \text{ m}^3$, or equivalent merit
Correct conversion of dimensions, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A total of 11 400 people entered a running race. The ratio of professional runners to amateurs was $3:16$. All the professional runners completed the race while 600 of the amateurs did not complete the race.

For those who completed the race, what is the ratio, in simplest form, of professional runners to amateurs?

solutions.latex:
Dividing 11 400 in the ratio $3:16$ (19 parts), one part is
$$\dfrac{11400}{19}=600$$
Professionals: $3\times 600=1800$. Amateurs: $16\times 600=9600$.

All professionals finished, and 600 amateurs did not, so $9600-600=9000$ amateurs finished.
$$1800:9000=1:5$$
So option B is correct.

$$\begin{aligned} 26\times 3000 &= 78\,000 \text{ cm} \\ &= 780 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
Speed over $12$ minutes:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Speed} &= \dfrac{780}{12} \\ &= 65 \text{ m/minute} \end{aligned}$$
Convert to km/h:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Speed} &= \dfrac{65\times 60}{1000} \text{ km/h} \\ &= 3.9 \text{ km/h} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A cake is constructed using a cylinder and a cone-shaped top. The cylinder has diameter 30 cm and height 6 cm.

\exfigure{40_q38_1}

The ratio of the volume of the cylinder to the volume of the cone-shaped top is $5:1$.

The cake is to be cut into equal slices with volume $212 \text{ cm}^3$.

How many equal slices can be cut from the cake?

solutions.latex:
The cylinder is 5 parts and the cone-shaped top is 1 part, so the cake is 6 parts.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Volume of cylinder} &= \pi\times 15^2\times 6 \\ &= 4241.150\ldots \text{ cm}^3 \\ &= 5\text{ parts} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Volume of cake} &= \dfrac{6}{5}\times 4241.150\ldots \\ &= 5089.38\ldots \text{ cm}^3 \end{aligned}$$

Each slice has volume $212 \text{ cm}^3$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number of slices} &= \dfrac{5089.38}{212} \\ &= 24.0065\ldots \\ &\approx 24 \end{aligned}$$

So 24 slices can be cut (to the nearest whole slice).
criteria: Calculates the volume of the cake, or equivalent merit
Calculates the volume of the cylinder, or equivalent merit

5959.stem: Andrew, Brandon and Cosmo are the first three batters in the school cricket team. In a recent match, Andrew scored 30 runs, Brandon scored 25 runs and Cosmo scored 40 runs.

parts.latex: What is the ratio of Andrew’s to Brandon’s to Cosmo’s runs scored, in simplest form?

In this match, the ratio of the total number of runs scored by Andrew, Brandon and Cosmo to the total number of runs scored by the whole team is $19:36$.

How many runs were scored by the whole team?

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Ratio} &= 30:25:40 \\ &= 6:5:8 \text{ (in simplest form)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Provides correct unsimplified ratio, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The total number of runs scored by Andrew, Brandon and Cosmo is $30+25+40=95$.

Let $x$ be the number of runs scored by the whole team.
$$19:36 = 95:x$$
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x}{95} &= \dfrac{36}{19} \\ x &= \dfrac{36}{19}\times 95 \\ &= 180 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore \text{The whole team scored } 180 \text{ runs}$$
criteria: Calculates the total runs for Andrew, Brandon and Cosmo, or equivalent merit

5982.stem:
A map is drawn to scale, on 1-cm grid paper, showing the positions of a supermarket and a cinema. A reservoir is also shown.

parts.latex: It takes 10 minutes to walk in a straight line from the cinema to the supermarket at a constant speed of 3 km/h. Show that the scale of the map is $1\text{ cm} = 100\text{ m}$.

The reservoir is initially empty. During a storm 20 mm of rain falls on the reservoir.

With the aid of one application of the trapezoidal rule, estimate the amount of water in the reservoir immediately after the storm. Assume that all rain which falls over the reservoir is stored. Give your answer in cubic metres.

solutions.latex:
Convert the speed to metres per minute:
$$3 \text{ km/h} = \dfrac{3000}{60} \text{ m/min}$$
In 10 minutes the walk is
$$\dfrac{3000}{60}\times 10 = 500 \text{ m}$$
On the map this distance is $5$ cm, so $5 \text{ cm} = 500 \text{ m}$.
$$\therefore\ 1 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Calculates correct actual distance ($500$ m), or equivalent merit
Provides a relevant conversion, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the scale $1 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ m}$ for the measurements, one application of the trapezoidal rule gives
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &\approx \dfrac{400}{2}(100 + 300) \\ &= 80\,000 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
The rainfall depth is $20 \text{ mm} = 0.02$ m, so
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Volume} &\approx 80\,000\times 0.02 \\ &= 1600 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates correct approximate area using trapezoidal rule, or equivalent merit
Provides a correct conversion, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A scientist is estimating the population of a bee colony.

The scientist captures $p$ bees but only marks $k\%$ of them and releases them all back into the colony. The next day, the scientist captures $q$ bees and finds that $r$ bees were marked.

Assuming all bees have an equal chance of being captured, which expression gives the best estimate of the total bee population?

solutions.latex:
Let $N$ be the total population. The number of marked bees is $k\%$ of $p$.
$$\text{marked}=\dfrac{kp}{100}$$
Assuming equal chance of capture, the proportion of marked bees in the second sample estimates the proportion in the whole colony.
$$\dfrac{r}{q}=\dfrac{kp}{100N}$$
Solve for $N$.
$$N=\dfrac{kpq}{100r}$$
Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
The perimeter of a rectangle is 390 cm and the side lengths are in the ratio $9:4$.

What is the area of the rectangle?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{5836_q28_s1}

Let the sides be $9x$ and $4x$. The perimeter is
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 9x + 4x + 9x + 4x \\ &= 26x \end{aligned}$$
Since $P = 390$:
$$\begin{aligned} 26x &= 390 \\ x &= \dfrac{390}{26} = 15 \end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Length} &= 9 \times 15 = 135 \\ \text{Width} &= 4 \times 15 = 60 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \text{Length} \times \text{Width} \\ &= 135 \times 60 \\ &= 8100 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the scale factor, or equivalent merit
Attempts to use the ratio, or equivalent merit

The ratio of the dimensions of a model car to the dimensions of an actual car is $1 : 64$. The actual car has a length of 4.9 m.

What is the length of the model car in cm, correct to 1 decimal place?

solutions.latex:
The model is $\dfrac{1}{64}$ of the actual length.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Actual length} &= 4.9 \text{ m} = 490 \text{ cm} \\ \text{Model length} &= \dfrac{490}{64} \\ &\approx 7.7 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the correct option is B.

parts.latex:
The population of snails in a garden is approximately 90.

One night Bobbie collected 18 snails from the garden. He tagged each snail and released it back into the garden.

The next night 20 snails were captured from the garden.

Approximately how many of the snails in the second sample are expected to have a tag?

solutions.latex:
The tagged fraction of the population is $\dfrac{18}{90}$, so expect that fraction of the second sample.
$$\dfrac{18}{90} \times 20 = 4 \text{ snails}$$
criteria: Provides a correct ratio for tagged snails, or equivalent merit
